This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation .

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 20.10.2019 while returning to his home from Muneshwara temple, nearby Mehaboob Sab Brick SCCH 5 Factory at about 2.30 p.m. at Pillagondahalli within the jurisiction of Bethamangala Police Station on his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04Y6231 slowly and cautiously, driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA01MB 4161 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against the petitioner and his motor cycle,
hence he fell down and sustained grievous injuries, so that, he has taken treatment at R.L.Jalappa Hospital and St.John's Medical College as indoor patient, spent an amount of Rs.6,00,000/.
3.
Prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, doing agricultural work and dairy farming, thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.

due to this accident he has lost his income and earning capacity, out of this accident crime No.134/2019 is registered against the said car and its driver before Bethamangala Police for the offences SCCH 5 punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.35,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a..
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared through his advocate but not filed written statement.

R2/insurer has appeared through his advocate and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, wherein admitted issuance of insurance policy bearing No.0516033118P110517595 in favour of car bearing Reg.No.KA04Y6231 and existence of insurance policy at the time of accident, taken contention that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c)
and 158(6) of M.V.Act, owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04Y6231 are necessary parties to this SCCH 5 petition, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170, Sec.147 and 149(2) of M.V.Act, driver of the car had no driving license at the time of accident, driver of the car is liable to prosecute under Sec.181 of M.V.Act, petitioner has to prove his age and income, claim made by the petitioner is higher side, hence petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:

sentences.text:
Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 20.10.2019 at about 2.35 p.m. on Bethamangala,
V.Kota, near Pillagondanahalli an Mehabobsab Brick Factory, due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing Reg.No.KA01MB4161 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
SCCH 5 2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 1 witness as PW2 and marked 19 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, R2 has deposed his evidence as RW1 and marked 2 documents as per Ex.R.1and Ex.R.2 and closed his evidence.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH 5 ::REASONS::
8.
Issue No.1

: As per story of the petitioner very accident is occurred due to negligency of driver of the car, owner of the car/R1 and R2/insurer have contested and taken contention that, there is no negligency of the car driver.

In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1,
in his chiefexamination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1.

copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of panchanama is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Wound Certificate is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of IMV report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
9.

In crossexamination there is no question by counsel for R2 by way of disputing the place, date and SCCH 5 time of the accident, but there is question that, very accident is occurred only due to negligency of the petitioner, but not by the negligency of the car driver, but such questions are denied by the petitioners.
10. On the other hand, R2 has deposed his evidence as RW1 and furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy marked as Ex.R.2.
R2 has also deposed his evidence stating that there is only negligency of the petitioner, but in cross examination admits that driver of the car had no driving licence at the time of accident.

It is noticed that, crime No.134/2019 before Bethamangala police is registered only against car driver as per Ex.P.1 on the basis of Ex.P.2, ultimately after investigation charge sheet is filed only against driver of the car by name Shaik Shafiulla for the Sri. sentences.text: Further it is noticed that as per Ex.P.8 said Shaik Shafivulla had admitted the guilt before the Magistrate Court, KGF in C.C.No.266/2020 and deposited the fine amount.
Further hand sketch map marked at Ex.P.4 speaks that, petitioner was on left side of his road and car has dashed against him and caused this accident.

Further it is noticed that, as per Ex.P.6 copy of IMV Report, motor cycle is damaged on front side and car is also damaged on front left side, it goes to show that, there is head on collusion, car driver has come on the road of the petitioner and dashed against him.
11. Under such circumstances, evidence available on record goes to show that, very accident is occurred only due to negligency of the car driver, but not by the petitioner.

Driver of the car is not examined by the R2, SCCH 5 R1/owner inspite of appearance before this court, not contested the petition by way of crossexamining the petitioner and deposing his evidence. During argument
counsel for R2 submitted that there is contributory negligence, but to consider his defence there is no sufficient evidence on record.
On the other hand, there is sufficient evidence of the petitioner to hold that, there is only negligency of the car driver.
Hence believing the version of the petitioner and disbelieving the version of the counsel for R2.
Hence, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:

As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained left foot crush injury and degloving injury over dorsum with 3 rd, 4th, 5th metatarsal fracture, for which he underwent debridement by plstic sugeryt, open reduction internal fixation, Kwiring for SCCH 5 3rd, 4th, 5th metatarsal fracture, debridement of left foot was done and debridement and SSG was done.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.5, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.9 issued by St.Johns Medical College Hospital wherein he has taken treatment as indoor patient since 21.10.2019 to 12.12.2019, 1 C.D. marked as Ex.P.14.
13.

Further Dr.Mahesh Shekoba, Orthopaedic Surgeon at St.John's Medical College Hospital has been examined as PW2 and furnished disability calculation sheet marked as Ex.P.16, OPD Record marked as Ex.P.17, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.18, case sheet marked as Ex.P.19 and he has assessed whole body disability at the rate of 11.7%.

14. In crossexamination this Doctor admits that, he has not treated the petitioner, only he has assessed SCCH 5 the disability, there are 3rd, 4th and 5th metatarsal fracture and there is no ankle fracture, fractures are united, but till today 4th toe is not united.
Further admits that, as per the norms in case of amputation to the great toe of the leg, disability is fixed at the rate of 5%.
Further admits that, there is no amputation of any toe.

Further admits that, for 3rd to 5th finger amputation disability is fixed at the rate of 3% each, except nonunion of 4 th toe there is no other complication,
further there is no fracture in ankle, but he has denied that there is no loss of movements in ankle joint, he denied that, disability assessed by him is higher side in order to help the petitioner.
On the other hand, there is no medical evidence of the respondents to disprove the case of the petitioners.

sentences.text: As per case of the petitioners, he was working as agriculturist and doing dairy farming, earning Rs.20,000/ p.m. but to prove the said fact he has not furnished any documents, discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9 speaks that, petitioner has taken treatment at St.Johns Medial College Hospital as indoor patient 21.10.2019 to 12.12.2019, borne medical bills of Rs.2,22,374/.
It all goes to show that, petitioner has taken long treatment in St.Johns hospital for injuries of his left leg fingers.
Doctor has assessed disability at the rate of 11% but said Doctor is not neither a treated Doctor nor a penalist of the medical board.
Further it is noticed that, he has not taken opinion from the treated Doctor and not gone through the case sheet.

Further very Doctor himself admitted that,
there was fractures to the SCCH 5 4th toe and now it is united, 3rd and 5th toes are not fractured.
16.

For amputation of the toe disability is fixed at the rate of 5%, but in the case on hand disability assessed by the Doctor is 11%, it goes to show that, disability assessed by the Doctor is higher side,
considering the injuries caused to the petitioner for all his 3 fingers, duration of the treatment,
expenditure borne by him, nature of work, for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income,
disability to the whole body is considered at the rate of 5%.

17. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 55 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.13, accordingly he is born on 01.01.1949 and the alleged accident is occurred on 20.10.2019, accordingly relying on Ex.P.13 his age is SCCH 5 considered about 70 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 5 is applicable with reference to Sarla Verma case.

18. As per his case, he was doing agriculture and dairy farming, thereby earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.,
to prove the said fact, he has produced copy of RTC Extracts marked as Ex.P.12.
In order to prove the dairy farming he has not furnished any documents.
As per case of the petitioners, he is agriculturist, there is no proof for fixed monthly income.

Under such circumstances, with reference to the year of accident, relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.14,000/ p.m.

Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/ is awarded, for loss of amenities of life Rs.15,000/ is awarded
, further he is entitled for Rs.14,000/ towards loss of income during laid up period.

Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation for medical expenses incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.10 for an amount of Rs.42,074/ SCCH 5 and Ex.P.11 for an amount of Rs.2,94,156/.

On perusal of the medical bills it is noticed that, petitioner had incurred total medical expenses of Rs.2,22,374/.

SCCH 5 22.

In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.0516033118P110517595, which is valid for the period from 14.11.2018 to 13.11.2019, the alleged accident was occurred on 20.10.2019, it reveals that, as on the date of accident insurance policy was in force.
Further driver of the car by name Shaik Shafivulla had no driving licence at the time of the accident.
Under such circumstances, naturally R1/owner is liable to pay the compensation in favour of petitioner, but

as per the observations made and findings given by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s. Swarna Singh and other reported in AIR 2004 SC 1531 and in case of Pappu and another V/s. Vinod Kumar Lamba and another reported in AIR 2018 SC 592, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and SCCH 5 necessary to issue directions against R2 Insurance Company to satisfy the petitioner by way of depositing the award amount within 60 days from the date of this order with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and recover from the R1/owner through process of law.
